title: One-use reservation
english:
ZAL version 1.
The machine is one_use.
The states are held, released, unseen.
The events are release, reserve.
The context observations are authorized.
Initially the state is unseen.
Each step is atomic. Only the control state may change.
Otherwise reject because unmatched and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r00: when the state is held and the event is release, if (not authorized), reject because unauthorized and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r01: when the state is held and the event is release, if authorized, move to released.
Rule r02: when the state is held and the event is reserve, if (not authorized), reject because unauthorized and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r03: when the state is held and the event is reserve, if authorized, reject because duplicate and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r04: when the state is released and the event is release, if (not authorized), reject because unauthorized and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r05: when the state is released and the event is release, if authorized, reject because not_held and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r06: when the state is released and the event is reserve, if (not authorized), reject because unauthorized and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r07: when the state is released and the event is reserve, if authorized, reject because duplicate and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r08: when the state is unseen and the event is release, if (not authorized), reject because unauthorized and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r09: when the state is unseen and the event is release, if authorized, reject because not_held and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r10: when the state is unseen and the event is reserve, if (not authorized), reject because unauthorized and keep the state unchanged.
Rule r11: when the state is unseen and the event is reserve, if authorized, move to held.
scope: One modeled request identity during one process lifetime. Supplied authorization is a Boolean observation. No authentication, persistence, concurrency, delivery, or liveness guarantee.
provenance: Read from the connected ZAL Abstraction Workspace using zal_layers on 2026-10-28. An illustrative site example; no human acceptance is asserted.
